vulnerable_code: val key = BuildConfig.API_KEY  // Vulnerable: extracted from APK\
secure_code: val key = getString(R.string.api_key)  // still in APK; use backend proxy / NDK  // Better: fetch at runtime\
patch:
--- a/Api.kt
+++ b/Api.kt
@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@
-val key = BuildConfig.API_KEY
+// Fetch from backend at runtime or use NDK obfuscation
+val key = fetchKeyFromBackend()\

title: Weak password hashing (MD5)

import java.security.SecureRandom
import org.mindrot.jbcrypt.BCrypt
def hashPw(pw: String) = BCrypt.hashpw(pw, BCrypt.gensalt(12))  // Secure
patch:
--- a/Auth.scala
+++ b/Auth.scala
@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@
-def hashPw(pw: String) = MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5").digest(pw.getBytes)

+def hashPw(pw: String) = BCrypt.hashpw(pw, BCrypt.gensalt(12))

title: Reflected XSS via flash message

flash("Hello " + request.args.get("name"))  # Vulnerable: reflected
return render_template("hi.html")
patch:

+++ b/views.py
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@

title: Path traversal in file download
description: A Spring controller builds a file path from a request parameter without canonicalization.
owasp_api: API3:2023 - Broken Object Property Level Authorization
root_cause: User input is used directly to construct filesystem paths without canonicalization or containment checks.
attack: name=../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files outside the intended directory.
impact: Disclosure of sensitive system or application files.
fix: Resolve and canonicalize the path, then verify it stays within the allowed base directory.
guideline: Canonicalize and contain: ensure resolved paths stay under the trusted root.

title: IDOR on invoice download
description: A Django view returns an object purely by its numeric id without checking ownership.
patch:
--- a/views.py
+++ b/views.py
@@ -3,6 +3,10 @@
-    inv = Invoice.objects.get(pk=invoice_id)
+    try:
+        inv = Invoice.objects.get(pk=invoice_id, user=request.user)
+    except Invoice.DoesNotExist:
+        raise Http404
root_cause: Object access is keyed only by an attacker-controllable identifier, not by caller ownership.
attack: User changes invoice_id from 1001 to 1002 and downloads another customer's invoice.
impact: Disclosure of other users' financial documents (PII, billing data).
fix: Always scope database queries by the authenticated principal (user/tenant).
guideline: Enforce object-level authorization on every record lookup.

title: Command injection via shell_exec
description: A Laravel controller passes user input to shell_exec.

title: Path traversal in file servlet
description: A Spring controller reads a file using a raw request path.
root_cause: Unsanitized path joined to base dir.
fix: Resolve and confine to base dir.
guideline: Confine file paths to a base directory.

title: Cross-site scripting in JSON response
description: A Rails API returns user input inside a JSON string rendered unsanitized in a page.
mitre_attack: T1059.007 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
vulnerable_code:
def comment
  render json: { text: params[:text] }  # Vulnerable if embedded in HTML later
end
secure_code:
def comment
  text = ERB::Util.html_escape(params[:text])  # Secure
  render json: { text: text }
end
patch:
--- a/comments_controller.rb
+++ b/comments_controller.rb
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
-def comment
-  render json: { text: params[:text] }
+  text = ERB::Util.html_escape(params[:text])
+  render json: { text: text }
root_cause: User input returned unescaped, later injected into DOM.
fix: Escape/encode on output; use safe DOM APIs.
guideline: Encode on output even in JSON consumed by pages.

title: Business logic: negative amount

vulnerable_code: acc.balance += req.amount;  // Vulnerable: negative allowed\

title: Reflected XSS in Play template
description: A Play Twirl template renders a request param with @ (unescaped) instead of @(...).
mitre_attack: T1059.007 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
vulnerable_code:
@(name: String)
Hello @name
secure_code:
@(name: String)
Hello @Html(name)
patch:
--- a/views/greet.scala.html +++ b/views/greet.scala.html @@ -1,2 +1,2 @@ -
Hello @name
+
Hello @Html(name)
root_cause: Twirl @name auto-escapes, but @Html(...) marks content as trusted raw HTML.
attack: name=<script>steal()</script> executes if ever passed through Html().
impact: XSS if misused; here the fix shows the correct escaped usage.
fix: Use default @ escaping; reserve @Html for vetted, sanitized markup only.
guideline: Default to escaped output in templates; avoid Html() on user input.

title: IDOR on resource read
description: A Play action returns a resource by id without ownership.
vulnerable_code: def show(id: Long) = Action { repo.find(id).map(Ok(_)).getOrElse(NotFound) }  // Vulnerable: no owner

title: Cryptographically weak random token
description: A Laravel app generates password-reset tokens with rand()/mt_rand(), which is predictable.
root_cause: A non-cryptographic PRNG is used for security-sensitive tokens, making them guessable.
attack: Attacker predicts the next mt_rand() value and resets another user's password.
impact: Account takeover via predictable reset tokens.
fix: Use a CSPRNG (random_bytes / Str::random) and store only a hash of the token.
guideline: Generate secrets with CSPRNGs; never use rand()/mt_rand() for tokens.

title: SSRF in Akka HTTP client call
description: An Akka HTTP service fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL without allowlisting.
patch:
--- a/ProxyController.scala
+++ b/ProxyController.scala
@@ -2,4 +2,8 @@
-  Http().singleRequest(HttpRequest(uri = url))
+  val allowed = Set("api.trusted.example")
+  val u = Uri(url)
+  if (u.scheme != "https" || !allowed.contains(u.authority.host.toString))
+    Future.successful(Forbidden)
+  else Http().singleRequest(HttpRequest(uri = u))
root_cause: Outbound requests follow attacker-controlled URLs with no host allowlist/egress control.
fix: Allowlist destinations, enforce HTTPS, block internal ranges.
guideline: Validate outbound URLs; block internal/metadata endpoints.

title: Secret exposed in operator log
description: An operator logs the full resource spec including a Secret reference's literal value.
owasp: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
patch:
--- a/operator.py
+++ b/operator.py
@@ -1,3 +1,6 @@
-    logging.info('spec=%s', req.obj['spec'])
+    def _redact(spec):
+        return {k: '***' if k.lower() in SENSITIVE else v for k, v in spec.items()}
+    logging.info('spec=%s', _redact(req.obj['spec']))
root_cause: Full resource specs containing secrets are written to logs.
attack: Anyone with log access reads secret values.
fix: Redact sensitive fields before logging; never log secrets.
guideline: Redact secrets in all logs; scrub sensitive keys.

title: Path traversal in static file handler
description: A Rust/Actix handler concatenates a request path to a base dir without canonicalization.
root_cause: Unvalidated path segments let ../ escape the intended directory.
attack: name=../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary files from the host.
fix: Canonicalize and verify the resolved path is contained within the base directory.
guideline: Join then contain: verify canonical path under the trusted root.

guideline: Compute prices server-side from authoritative sources.

title: Insecure redirect after OAuth with no state
description: A Rails OAuth callback does not verify the state parameter.
vulnerable_code:
def oauth_callback
  # Vulnerable: no state check
  user = User.from_omniauth(request.env['omniauth.auth'])
  session[:user_id] = user.id
end
secure_code:
def oauth_callback
  if session[:oauth_state] != params[:state]  # Secure
    return head :bad_request
  end
  user = User.from_omniauth(request.env['omniauth.auth'])
  session[:user_id] = user.id
end
patch:
--- a/callbacks_controller.rb
+++ b/callbacks_controller.rb
@@ -1,5 +1,7 @@
-def oauth_callback
-  user = User.from_omniauth(request.env['omniauth.auth'])
+def oauth_callback
+  if session[:oauth_state] != params[:state]
+    return head :bad_request
+  end
+  user = User.from_omniauth(request.env['omniauth.auth'])
root_cause: Missing state verification enables OAuth CSRF login.
attack: Attacker initiates login linking victim to attacker's account.
fix: Generate and verify a state parameter per round trip.
guideline: Verify OAuth state; use PKCE for public clients.

title: Stack-based buffer overflow in HTTP header parse
description: An embedded web server copies a header value into a fixed stack buffer without bounds.
root_cause: strcpy into a fixed buffer allows overflow with a long header value.
attack: Send a huge header to overflow the stack and hijack execution.
impact: Remote code execution on the device.
fix: Use bounded copies (strncpy + NUL) or length-checked parsers.
guideline: Avoid strcpy; bound all copies; compile with stack protectors.

def up(req):

  ext = os.path.splitext(f.name)[1].lower()
  if ext not in ALLOWED: return HttpResponse('bad type', 415)  # Secure
  name = secrets.token_hex(16) + ext
  with open('/media/'+name, 'wb') as o: o.write(f.read())
patch:
--- a/views.py
+++ b/views.py
@@ -1,4 +1,8 @@
-  with open('/media/'+f.name, 'wb') as o: o.write(f.read())

+  if ext not in ALLOWED: return HttpResponse('bad type', 415)
+  name = secrets.token_hex(16) + ext
+  with open('/media/'+name, 'wb') as o: o.write(f.read())
fix: Allowlist extensions; randomize name; store outside exec context.

title: Session fixation in Spring
description: Spring login does not configure session fixation protection.
vulnerable_code: http.formLogin();
secure_code:
http.sessionManagement()
    .sessionFixation().migrateSession();

title: Buffer overflow in strcpy
description: A C function copies input with strcpy into a fixed buffer.

title: Excessive data exposure
description: Endpoint returns full ORM object including secrets.
patch:
--- a/me.py
+++ b/me.py
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
-async def me(u: User = Depends(current)):
-    return u
+async def me(u: User = Depends(current)):
+    return UserPublic.from_orm(u)

title: CORS allow-all with credentials
description: CORS permits any origin with credentials.
vulnerable_code: .allowed_origin(Origin::star())  // Vulnerable + credentials\
secure_code: .allowed_origin(Origin::exact("https://app.example.com".parse().unwrap()))  // Secure\
patch:
--- a/cors.rs
+++ b/cors.rs
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@
-.allowed_origin(Origin::star())
+.allowed_origin(Origin::exact("https://app.example.com".parse().unwrap()))\

title: No rate limit on password reset
description: A Django password reset has no rate limit, enabling account enumeration/abuse.
patch:
--- a/views.py
+++ b/views.py
@@ -1,3 +1,6 @@
-  send_reset(req.POST['email'])
+  if is_ratelimited(req, group='reset', key='ip', rate='3/m', method=ALL):
+    return HttpResponse('slow down', 429)
+  send_reset(req.POST['email'])
attack: Mass reset emails; enumerate valid accounts.

title: Path traversal in file open
description: A C++ service opens a file whose path is built from a request parameter.
root_cause: User input builds filesystem paths without canonicalization/containment.
fix: Canonicalize and verify the path stays under the base directory.
guideline: Resolve and contain; verify under trusted root.

title: SQL injection via string format
description: An Actix handler builds a query by formatting.
vulnerable_code: let q = format!("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{}''", name);\nsqlx::query(&q).fetch_all(&pool).await  // Vulnerable\
secure_code: sqlx::query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1").bind(&name).fetch_all(&pool).await  // Secure: bound\
patch:
--- a/handler.rs
+++ b/handler.rs
@@ -1,3 +1,2 @@
-let q = format!("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{}''", name);
-sqlx::query(&q).fetch_all(&pool).await
+sqlx::query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1").bind(&name).fetch_all(&pool).await\

title: IDOR on resource read
description: A handler returns a resource by id without owner check.
vulnerable_code:
let inv = repo.find_invoice(id).await?;  // Vulnerable: no owner
Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(inv))
secure_code:
let inv = repo.find_invoice_for(id, user_id).await?;  // Secure: scoped
Ok(HttpResponse::Ok().json(inv))
